question.text: The Price-to-Book (P/B) ratio is MOST commonly used for valuing:

explanation.text: The Logic: The source workbook states that the P/B ratio is widely used for valuing financial-services and banking stocks where assets closely follow market value, which is what the keyed option captures. The Trap: Software startups carry mostly intangible assets that book value does not capture well. Oil and gas futures are derivative contracts, not equity claims. Commodity miners are typically valued on reserves and cash flows rather than P/B alone. Note: Only the banking and financial-services suitability of P/B is anchored to the cited page; any specific tangible-book or goodwill adjustment guidance requires a separately cited source.
